title: Colimit resolutions from bounded-above resolutions of good truncations
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] admitting sequential colimits indexed by the positive integers, which preserve short exact sequences of diagrams [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\mathcal P$ be a class of objects containing $0$, closed under finite direct sums, such that every object of $\mathcal A$ is an epimorphic image of an object of $\mathcal P$. Define $\overline{\mathcal P}=\{M:\text{there exist }P\in\mathcal P\text{ and an isomorphism }P\cong M\}$. This class contains every zero object, is stable under isomorphisms and finite biproducts, and every object is an epimorphic image of an object in it. For every $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complex $K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], put $T_n=\tau_{\le n}K$ for $n\ge1$, where $T_n^i=K^i$ for $i<n$, $T_n^n=\ker d_K^n$ and $T_n^i=0$ for $i>n$, with induced differentials. There exist bounded above complexes $E_n$ with terms in $\overline{\mathcal P}$, transitions $u_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$, and quasi-isomorphisms $r_n:E_n\to T_n$ such that $r_{n+1}u_n=j_nr_n$ strictly, where $j_n:T_n\to T_{n+1}$ is the canonical inclusion. Write $E=\varinjlim_n E_n$ for their termwise colimit and $e_n:E_n\to E$ for its legs. The induced chain map $a:E\to K$, characterized by $ae_n=(T_n\to K)r_n$, is a quasi-isomorphism. Moreover $H^j(E_n)=0$ for $j>n$, and $H^j(e_n)$ is an isomorphism for $j\le n$.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, second paragraph, colimit resolution of an arbitrary complex; Tag 06XX, lemma-special-direct-system. Isomorphism closure makes the existing 06XX formulation applicable.

proof.text: The isomorphism closure $\overline{\mathcal P}$ is stable under isomorphisms by composition. Every zero object is isomorphic to the given $0\in\mathcal P$. If $M\cong P$ and $N\cong Q$ with $P,Q\in\mathcal P$, then $M\oplus N\cong P\oplus Q$, and the latter belongs to $\mathcal P$; iterating includes the empty biproduct. Finally an original cover $P\twoheadrightarrow M$ is already a cover from $\overline{\mathcal P}$. Thus this class satisfies all hypotheses of the compatible-resolution theorem.

source.place: Tag 06XX, lemma-special-direct-system, hypotheses on the class; isomorphism-closure bookkeeping.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-truncation-resolution-system] to $K$ and $\overline{\mathcal P}$, using Step 1. Its statement gives bounded above complexes $E_n$ with all terms in this class, quasi-isomorphisms $r_n:E_n\to T_n$ and transitions $u_n$ with $r_{n+1}u_n=j_nr_n$ as actual chain maps, for every $n\ge1$. Its additional termwise epimorphism and split-monomorphism conclusions are unnecessary here. No colimit or exactness assumption is needed for this application.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, second paragraph, invocation of Tag 06XX (lemma-special-direct-system).

proof.text: Write $h_n:T_n\to K$ for the canonical inclusion. From the displayed truncation terms, $\ker d_{T_n}^j/\operatorname{im}d_{T_n}^{j-1}$ identifies via $h_n$ with $H^j(K)$ when $j<n$. For $j=n$, the differential out of $\ker d_K^n$ is zero and the incoming image is the image of $d_K^{n-1}$ inside this kernel, so the same conclusion holds. For $j>n$ the term is zero and the cohomology is zero. Since $r_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $H^j(E_n)=0$ for $j>n$, and $c_n=H^j(h_nr_n)$ is an isomorphism for $j\le n$. The strict squares and $h_{n+1}j_n=h_n$ give $c_{n+1}H^j(u_n)=c_n$.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, second paragraph, cohomology of the good truncations.

proof.text: For each $i$ take $E^i=\varinjlim_{n\ge1}E_n^i$ with legs $e_n^i$. The compatible maps $e_n^{i+1}d_{E_n}^i$ induce $d_E^i:E^i\to E^{i+1}$. Composing $d_E^{i+1}d_E^i$ with every $e_n^i$ gives zero, hence it is zero by colimit uniqueness. Thus $E$ is a complex and the $e_n$ are chain maps. Any compatible family of chain maps out of the $E_n$ factors degreewise through $E$; its differential equations hold after precomposition with all legs, hence hold on $E$. This proves that this termwise cocone is also a colimit in complexes. The maps $h_nr_n$ are compatible by Step 2, so they induce a unique chain map $a:E\to K$, with $ae_n=h_nr_n$.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, second paragraph, termwise colimit and its augmentation.

proof.text: Apply [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] to the small category of positive integers with its usual order, to cochain shape on $\mathbf Z$, and to the diagram $E_n$. The required colimits and their exactness are exactly the assumptions of this item. Consequently, for every integer $j$, $(H^j(E),H^j(e_n))$ is a colimit cocone of the diagram $H^j(E_n)$. The map induced by the compatible maps $c_n$ of Step 3 is precisely $H^j(a)$, because $H^j(a)H^j(e_n)=c_n$.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, second paragraph: exact sequential colimits commute with cohomology.

proof.text: Fix $j$ and set $N=\max(1,j)$. The cocone $(H^j(K),c_n)$ is itself colimiting. Indeed, for any compatible cocone $b_n:H^j(E_n)\to B$, its unique factorization is $b_Nc_N^{-1}:H^j(K)\to B$. For $n\le N$, compose the transitions from $n$ to $N$ and use the cocone equations to obtain $(b_Nc_N^{-1})c_n=b_n$. For $n\ge N$, write $v:H^j(E_N)\to H^j(E_n)$ for the transition; then $c_nv=c_N$, so $v=c_n^{-1}c_N$ and the same equation follows from $b_nv=b_N$. Uniqueness follows by precomposing with the isomorphism $c_N$. By Step 5 and uniqueness of colimits, $H^j(a)$ is therefore an isomorphism. This holds for every $j$, so $a$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Finally, when $j\le n$, $H^j(a)H^j(e_n)=c_n$ is an isomorphism by Step 3; since $H^j(a)$ is invertible, so is $H^j(e_n)$. Together with Step 3 this proves both final assertions.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, second paragraph, eventual cohomology identification and its colimit legs.

Statement checked against Stacks derived.tex 0794 (second paragraph) and 06XX. The statement is byte-identical to the one in Q151 snapshots a2594/ac1c/2a42/419a, and stmt_deps are unchanged. The 0794 paragraph needs exact sequential colimits only in A; F and B are used later in 0794. Item asserts the boundary case j=n, which holds since T_n^n=ker d^n. Step 1: the isomorphism closure P̄ gives every hypothesis of lem-sfb-subcategory-truncation-resolution-system (zero objects, stable under isomorphism and finite biproducts, covers). Step 2: that node's statement gives E_n, the strict squares and the quasi-isomorphisms for n>=1. Step 3: H^j(T_n) checked for j<n (kernel unchanged because ker d^n is a subobject of K^n), j=n and j>n, so c_{n+1}H(u_n)=c_n. Step 4: the termwise colimit is a colimit in complexes, checked on the legs. Step 5: src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits holds for any I and shape when colimits are exact, and H^j(a)H^j(e_n)=c_n. Step 6: with N=max(1,j), b_N c_N^{-1} is the unique factorization, so H^j(a) and then H^j(e_n) (j<=n) are isomorphisms; no circularity. Edge cases tested: K=0, K in degree 0, n or n+1, j very negative, P without every zero object. Duplicate search (rg -L over 06XX/0794/special-direct-system; flat/K-flat towers, good-truncation-stage-naturality, resolution-colimit-quasi-isos, resolving-class-derived-descent) found no node stating the item. No new nodes; Mathlib searches are logged in all three kinds; proof_deps equals the union of uses; no SGA. The parent's re-split assigned old steps 1/3/4 here, and all three are carried.
